# Help people understand and revise a plan

Make a planning application's timing, trade-offs and revisions understandable.
Provide a readable timeline and a textual equivalent. Develop separately reasoned
solution choices under the owner's outcomes and use feedback to guide the next
planning decision. Each current graph describes its desired product and actual
realization; Git records its evolution.

# Make timing readable

Show task names and date ranges alongside aligned timeline bars. Provide textual
dates, keyboard-accessible controls and horizontal scrolling for long plans.

# Validate input and render project text literally

Treat names/imported data as text. Validate a candidate before replacing the saved
plan and show actionable input errors while retaining valid work and editable drafts.
The browser uses textContent and ordinary native controls for project strings.

# Keep intentions, conclusions and implementation separately revisable

Record coherent owner outcomes separately from reasoned realization choices and
implementation mappings. Agent planning reads saved context/impact and produces
positive current-state specification before code. Owner-authorized redirects are
planned explicitly; commit reasons and predecessor Git trees retain removed branches.
Implementation deepens existing intentions and reports scope gaps for owner planning.

# Plan a business portfolio

Help a manager see multiple business projects together with each task assigned to
a project. The local prototype explores a readable portfolio calendar and task table;
shared service and capacity scheduling are independently scoped follow-on outcomes.

# Forecast business-day prerequisite timing

Forecast task dates from positive workday durations and finish-to-start prerequisites.
Use Monday–Friday working days and preserve understandable task-level date results.

# Identify responsible team members

Record and display the named member responsible for each task. Make responsibility
readable alongside project membership and task timing. Capacity scheduling has a
separately scoped realization under its own requirement.

# Plan a capacity-aware extension

A follow-on scheduler should delay work when the same team member is booked twice.
Keep this outcome independently revisable from the initial local calendar prototype.
The prototype's delivered subset is task responsibility display and dependency timing;
owner planning determines the capacity extension's delivery.

# Summarize portfolio completion

Show project completion summaries alongside the task-level view. Make the summary's
calculation understandable and keep individual tasks and progress values inspectable.

# Plan a controlled shared-workspace extension

A follow-on shared workspace should let authenticated accounts share plans with
controlled access and centralized persistence. Scope service operation/privacy and
permissions independently from the delivered local read-only calendar experiment.
Owner planning determines this extension's delivery and operating constraints.

# Read project and portfolio finish timing

Show predicted finish dates for projects and the whole portfolio through the task
calendar and project summaries. Explain them as dependency-based forecasts.

# Use whole UTC weekdays for the portfolio forecast

Parse real ISO calendar dates as UTC whole days. Normalize project start to the
next Monday–Friday workday. Process all prerequisite relationships topologically;
each task starts at the latest normalized project start or next weekday after all
predecessor finishes. Its positive duration includes its first workday.

Validate unique nonempty task IDs, durations 1–100, finite progress 0–100 and
prerequisite arrays/references. Reject cycles and invalid calendar dates. Preserve
input order in returned rows and keep source task data unchanged. The prototype
calendar consists of weekdays; holiday/resource extensions require their own scope.

# Separate a shared HTTP and relational-service choice

For the planned authenticated workspace, use an HTTP service with relational plan
storage as a separately reviewable design direction. Before service implementation,
owner planning fixes account permissions, hosting/privacy and operating scope.
The local prototype provides read-only browser data and its own implementation
mapping; this service choice remains explicitly follow-on specification.

# Calculate inspectable project rollups

Group forecast tasks by project. Show each project's latest task end date and the
rounded unweighted arithmetic mean of its completion values. Retain count and task
rows so the metric is inspectable as a simple task-completion summary.

# Scope a greedy capacity pass as a separate extension

A candidate capacity extension orders tasks and delays each owner's work after
basic dependency forecasting. Owner planning must choose ordering/ties and resource
calendar constraints before implementation. Keep the extension separate from the
current date model; the local prototype's realized subset is dependency scheduling
and owner labels. Assess greedy-result quality under its declared ordering.

# Compute the local portfolio forecast and rollups

`model.js` implements validated UTC weekday prerequisite timing and project finish/
mean-progress rollups over local demo data. Task responsibility is a displayed field.
`test/model.test.cjs` covers weekend boundaries, order independence, malformed data,
cycles/missing references and rollup semantics. The delivered scope is the pure
calendar/summary experiment; capacity and shared-service extensions have separate
planned specifications and realization boundaries.

# Render a local read-only portfolio timeline

Local classic scripts, native text and CSS show project summaries, task/owner/date/
progress rows and aligned timeline bars. `index.html` opens directly or through a
local static server. The displayed plan is the prototype's bundled local demo.
Syntax/model checks support the calendar experiment; browser interaction coverage
is assessed independently for each delivered stage.

# Plan one personal renovation

Help one person plan a home renovation with local task dates, priorities and a
readable timeline. The person owns the complete plan in this browser and JSON file.

# Let the person choose every task date

The person enters each task's start and end date explicitly. Saving a task changes
that task's chosen range while preserving all other task dates. Show understandable
inclusive dates in the timeline and table.

# Identify personal task priorities

Provide low, normal and high priority labels. Keep each task's priority readable
alongside its manually selected range in the timeline and textual view.

# Keep a portable validated JSON plan

Import/export a documented versioned JSON format. Validate imports before applying
them. Explain format conversion and information losses in a preview, with explicit
replacement of current work. Export saved valid plan data for owner-controlled files.

# Save valid work in this browser

Autosave valid edits in browser-local storage when available. Explain session-only
operation and storage failures. Keep a portable JSON export so the owner can save
work independently of browser storage conditions.

# Give personal tasks independent date ranges

Each task has its own manually chosen date range. Its edits preserve the date ranges
of all other tasks. The person's timeline expresses those chosen appointments.

# Validate inclusive manual UTC calendar ranges

Parse real ISO dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31 as UTC whole days. End is at
or after start. Inclusive span is end-start+1, including same-day/weekend tasks.
All tasks together fit at most 730 calendar days. Preserve the entered ranges
and task input order while validating a candidate plan.

# Autosave through localStorage with protected original bytes

Use browser localStorage for validated plan autosave under a stable local origin.
Storage failures leave the app usable in memory with visible session-only/export
guidance. Unreadable saved bytes stay protected until explicit reset or a supported
preview/Apply replacement. Browser-local persistence has browser/origin/storage
lifecycle conditions; exported files provide owner-controlled portability.

# Define version-one manual-plan JSON

A `version: 1` envelope contains title and tasks. Tasks have unique IDs, title,
start/end ISO dates and low/normal/high priority. Use at most 100 tasks, IDs of
1–40 letters/numbers/_/-, and trimmed nonempty names/title up to 120 characters.
Validate real bounded dates, ordered inclusive ranges and a 730-day chart horizon
before applying import. Return normalized copied fields in entered task order.

# Validate independent inclusive personal dates

`model.js` normalizes version-one title/tasks, validates IDs/priorities/calendar
ranges and bounded chart data, and computes inclusive spans. Input data remains
unchanged and saved ranges remain independent. Model tests cover same-day/weekend
ranges, order independence, JSON round-trip and invalid data. The exported demo
in `history/personal-v1.json` supplies an inspectable portable-plan fixture.

# Edit and store a local personal timeline

Native forms create/edit/delete manual ranges and priorities. A horizontally
scrolling chart and date table show every calendar day. Validated saves autosave
locally; failed storage/loading stays session-only with protected bytes until reset.
JSON export downloads a file; confirmed imports validate before replacing the plan.
Project strings use textContent. Model/syntax tests supply bounded prototype evidence;
browser storage and interaction have their own verification scope.

# Plan one makerspace workshop

Help a makerspace organize one workshop using work durations, prerequisites,
earliest bounds and an explicit what-if baseline. Keep the plan local and portable.

# Forecast dates from whole workday durations

Enter positive Monday–Friday workday durations. Calculate each task's forecast
start/end and recalculate related timing after valid edits. Explain forecasts as
planning estimates under the declared calendar and prerequisite rules.

# Respect finish-to-start prerequisites

Allow tasks to reference distinct existing prerequisites in an acyclic graph.
A successor's start follows every prerequisite's finish. Surface invalid links or
cycles before applying a candidate and retain the saved valid plan.

# Respect project and task earliest-start bounds

Use the project start and optional per-task earliest date as lower bounds for the
forecast. Weekend lower bounds advance to Monday. Explain calculated dates as
forecasts satisfying these bounds and prerequisite timing.

# Use an explicit Monday–Friday workshop calendar

Count whole Monday–Friday workdays and show weekend shading on the complete calendar
axis. The declared forecast model is weekday work duration and prerequisites.
Holiday calendars, partial days and resource availability are separately scoped
planning extensions.

# Compare a what-if with a deliberately captured baseline

Capture a full validated saved-plan baseline on explicit request. Edit the current
plan and compare current/baseline dates visually and textually. Keep that baseline
immutable across ordinary edits. Replacing or clearing it is an explicit action.

# Edit a validated complete workshop task set

Use accessible native forms to add, select, edit and remove tasks. Save a candidate
only after validating durations, bounds and prerequisites. A referenced prerequisite
can be removed after the user explicitly edits its dependents' links. Invalid edits
and cancelled navigation retain the draft and saved valid plan.

# Preview personal-file conversion before replacing work

Support portable version-one manual-plan import through a preview of its version-two
workshop conversion. Explain date/priority losses and weekday forecasting semantics
before explicit Apply. Keep current saved work/storage intact during preview/cancel.

# Calculate bounded UTC weekday DAG forecasts iteratively

Use whole UTC dates and iterative topological processing of all prerequisites.
Start is the maximum of normalized project start, normalized optional earliest and
next weekday after each predecessor end. End is duration-1 workdays after start.
Return rows in saved task order and preserve inputs.

Validate up to 100 tasks, durations 1–60 whole workdays, real ISO dates 2000–2100,
unique 1–40 character letter/number/_/- task IDs, trimmed title/names of 1–120
characters and distinct existing non-self prerequisites. Reject cyclic or invalid
candidates. Earliest may be null/empty. Current and baseline together fit an
inclusive axis of at most 730 calendar days; include normalized starts and all
forecast rows in its bounds. The model is a small deterministic dependency forecast.

# Store an explicit deep baseline and compare on a common axis

Capture a copied normalized full saved plan on request. Current edits retain it.
Forecast current and baseline independently, then render both on the same bounded
calendar axis. Use current task order followed by baseline-only tasks. Show textual
start/end and finish delta in calendar days. Baseline-only rows remain visible as
removed; new current-only tasks show Added; absent baseline dates show an empty
comparison. Replace/clear actions are explicit and validation preserves snapshots.

# Define version-two workshop JSON and previewed conversion

A `version: 2` envelope has title/start/tasks and optional full baseline. Tasks have
id/title/duration/earliest/dependsOn. Normalize copied fields, validate both forecasts
and their common axis, and serialize saved data. Import preview accepts up to one
million characters; file input is bounded to one million bytes. Apply explicitly
replaces saved work/storage after confirmation; cancel retains both.

Convert valid version-one ranges to the count of contained weekdays, minimum one
workday; keep each old start as earliest, create empty prerequisite arrays and an
empty baseline, and use the earliest task start as project start (2026-04-06 for
an empty plan). Consume the v1 priority as conversion input and report its omission.
Warn that manual end becomes a duration-derived forecast and weekend-only ranges
advance to a workday. Keep stored v1 bytes protected pending preview/Apply/reset.

# Use local classic scripts, native forms and a DOM calendar

Use dependency-free local classic scripts, textContent and native controls. Launch
from local files or a stable local static origin. The latter supplies predictable
browser-local storage conditions; file-origin failures show session-only guidance.

Render a horizontally scrolling calendar with weekend shading, distinct current/
baseline bars and a text date table. Keep scrolling inside chart/table areas and
retain form/caret during resize. Preview file/pasted JSON separately from saved data,
cancel stale asynchronous file reads, and confirm discard of dirty task/settings
input before replacement/navigation. Browser task prerequisites express scheduling;
specspec graph links express specification justification.

# Calculate workshop forecasts, baseline snapshots and JSON previews

`model.js` implements iterative UTC weekday DAG scheduling, bounded normalization,
immutable copied baselines, current/baseline rows and calendar-day deltas. Task save
validates the whole candidate; removal validates reference safety. Import returns a
validated version-two preview or explicit version-one conversion warnings.

Model tests cover seeded DAGs against an independent reference, deep bounded graphs,
weekend/DST/leap dates, invalid/cyclic inputs, input/baseline immutability and the
archived personal JSON fixture. The pure model has deterministic local-data semantics.

# Edit and persist a native local workshop calendar

`app.js`, local markup and styles implement current/baseline bars, date table,
weekend shading, editable prerequisites and explicit baseline capture/replace/clear.
Valid edits autosave. Corrupt/v1 saved bytes remain downloadable and protected
until Apply/reset. Import preview and cancelled/stale reads retain saved work.
Dirty failed drafts and native caret persist through invalid edits and resize.

Project strings use textContent. Real-browser checks cover forecasts, baselines,
cyclic drafts, safe task deletion, literal markup, downloads/uploads, conversion
preview/cancel/Apply, reload, protected/denied storage and direct-file launch. Model
and browser seams provide reproducible bounded checks for this local planner.

# Map the specification workflow to actual Git and CLI artifacts

`history/cli.jsonl` records actual current-CLI graph writes/ancestor-query/dependent/validation
results. `revisions.json` records real stage commits and receipt ordinals. Agent
specification commits precede runnable code and implementation mappings. Redirect
commit messages explain deletion scope; predecessor trees retain earlier reasoning.

# Map the specification workflow to actual Git and CLI artifacts

`history/cli.jsonl` records actual current-CLI graph writes/ancestor-query/dependent/validation
results. `revisions.json` records real stage commits and receipt ordinals. Agent
specification commits precede runnable code and implementation mappings. Redirect
commit messages explain deletion scope; predecessor trees retain earlier reasoning.

The complete independent bundle supplies staged/history experiments. The verifier
checks every retained ref, positive current-stage records, exact indexes, receipt
contents, ordering, semantic/edge/source deltas and runnable models. Staged full-blob
source anchors use strict/expanding regions retained by corresponding code trees.
The tracked snapshot is a portable fixture; external clones own Git workspaces.
Optional narrative illustrates product briefs; actual artifacts supply evidence.
